tasks.short: Review workflow charts of computer tasks

steps.what: Review workflow charts the programmer analyst drew
List computer tasks such as updating records

loop.output: one row per label that names a computer task
loop.check: Each row cites a step label on the chart
loop.stop: Leave a blank label for the analyst and stop after one pass
loop.why_not_simpler: A label such as update records can mean several writes, so a keyword is not the task

steps.what: Ask the analyst where a chart is unclear
Explain the computer tasks on that chart
Sign what the computer tasks will update

tasks.design: The programmer analyst files workflow charts in {DOCS}. The administrator reviews them to understand the tasks the computer will perform, such as updating records. A short list may be drafted from the chart labels. The administrator signs what those tasks will update. Nobody changes the database from the chart alone.
tasks.previous_blocker: Charts arrived as pictures in mail, so a task could not be named or questioned.
tasks.enabler_now: A chart can carry step labels that a list can cite.
tasks.still_hard: What the computer will really do, when a label is vague, is still a conversation with the analyst.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator decides which chart steps are understood and signs that reading.
tasks.altitude: Less time redrawing the chart. Understanding the tasks stays with the administrator and the analyst.

reach.task: Explain a chart step the administrator marked unclear
reach.learn: Which step ids are still open

evidence.claim: Reading a workflow chart is a list of tasks plus a conversation where a label is unclear. The picture is not the understanding.
Digest [S3] says a prompt can fill document fields and can be wrong. A task list drafted from chart labels is checked by the administrator.

assumptions: Focal role is the database administrator. The analyst drew the charts. Changing the database is a different task.
Input contract: chart id, step label, record name. Producer is the programmer analyst. A chart with no step labels is read by hand and marked manual.
Use the document store before a custom diagram tool.
research_questions: How often does the analyst's explanation change the first reading of a chart?

already_counted.description: The first reading of the charts stays with the administrator
The conversation with the analyst stays

incremental.description: Ask for a new chart when step labels are missing

approvals.approved_version: reading signed for these chart step ids

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes charts have no step labels, so the list is useless and the meeting stays as it is. The high case saves only the first transcription. The conversation and the sign-off are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Open the company definition in the dictionary
Revise the company definition from the request

loop.output: a draft that changes only requested fields
loop.check: Unrequested sentences stay as they were
loop.stop: Stop if the request names no field
loop.why_not_simpler: Whether the new wording matches real use is not in the request

steps.what: Judge whether the definition still matches use
Sign the company definition of the data
Store the signed definition in the dictionary

tasks.design: A request names the company definition that should change in the data dictionary on {DOCS}. A draft may revise only the fields the request names. The administrator judges whether the definition still matches how the data is used, then signs one version. That version is stored. Applying it to live objects is a separate signed change, not this filing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Definitions were edited in place, so the previous company meaning could not be restored.
tasks.enabler_now: The dictionary can hold a version, an owner, and the request id.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the new definition matches real use is a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator revises the wording only by signing the definition.

ambition.what: Sign a dictionary change when the use is clear, not in a yearly cleanup

tasks.altitude: Less time finding the old definition. The company meaning of the data stays a signed decision.

reach.task: Confirm the use before the definition is signed

evidence.claim: A data dictionary change is a request, a revised definition, and a person who signs the company meaning. The screen edit is not the decision.
Digest [S3] says a prompt can fill document fields and can be wrong. The revised definition is checked against the request and the stated use.
Digest [S28] keeps an unattended write to a production database out of scope. Storing the signed definition does not apply it to live objects.

assumptions: Focal role is the database administrator. Owners confirm use. They do not sign the definition.
Input contract: dictionary id, current definition, requested change, use note. Producer is the requester. A request with no use note is not signed.
Use the document store's versioning before a custom dictionary.
unknowns: Which definitions are still used by a report.
research_questions: How often does the signed definition differ from the request?

already_counted.description: Reading the current definition stays with the administrator
Judging the use stays with the administrator

incremental.description: Mark a definition unused when no report cites it

approvals.approved_version: definition signed for this dictionary id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes requests lack a use note, so the draft is discarded. The high case assumes clean requests, but every definition is still judged and signed. Applying the definition to live objects is not counted here.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The administrator stops retyping chart notes and dictionary lines, and spends the time on what the computer will actually do and what the company definition of data should say.
reach: The programmer analyst hears which chart step was unclear.
Owners receive a signed dictionary version instead of an edited copy in mail.
skills_to_grow: Read a workflow chart as a list of computer tasks, not as a picture to admire.
Change a dictionary definition only by signing a version.
Treat a drafted definition as unchecked until it matches the use.
role.ambitious_version: Every chart review ends in a signed note of the tasks, and every dictionary change has one signed definition.
